_doc: Timed jobs: on some flight days your ship has one job that finishes at a set local time ('around 14:15'). The job, its finish time and its outcome are all fixed by the voyage key, the day and the ship (lv/engage.py), so every ship agrees and nothing waits for anyone. The time only decides when the phone shows the result. h = [earliest, latest) finish hour, local. out: w = weight, t = result text, art = artifact unlocked. {A} = your astronaut. STUBS: the content pass replaces these.

jobs.label: EVA
jobs.t: {A} suits up to swap a sticking radiator latch on the aft skirt.

out.t: Latch swapped. {A} is back inside with oxygen to spare and an opinion about the old latch.
The latch was fine. The bracket behind it had walked two millimetres. {A} shims it and photographs it for the ground.
Behind the latch, {A} finds a micrometeoroid lodged in the insulation, smaller than a grain of rice. It goes in a sample bag, labelled and dated.

jobs.label: Calibration
jobs.t: The star tracker needs a full recalibration: six hours of slews, one star at a time.

out.t: It converges on the third pass. The residuals are small enough to brag about, so {A} does.
It converges only after {A} notices the reference star is a variable star. The catalogue gets a quiet correction.

jobs.label: Tank survey
jobs.t: {A} runs the weekly boil-off survey on the header tanks.

out.t: Boil-off is 0.3% under the model. The model takes the credit.
{A} traces a warm spot on the header tank to a heater relay that sticks on. It's tagged out, bypassed and written up before dinner.

jobs.label: Filter swap
jobs.t: Water recovery is due a filter swap. The procedure says 40 minutes. It is never 40 minutes.

out.t: Two hours and one spare O-ring later, the water tastes of nothing at all, which is the goal.
The old filter is clogged with something fibrous. {A} bags a sample for the ground and starts a list of suspects.
Taped inside the old filter housing: a 1969 quarter and a note. 'For luck. R.' Nobody on the manifest starts with R.

jobs.label: Antenna check
jobs.t: A pointing check on the high-gain antenna, timed for the next Earth pass.

out.t: Pointing error under a tenth of a degree. The ground replies 22 minutes later with one word: nice.
Off by half a degree. {A} finds a thermal offset nobody had modelled and writes it into the table by hand.
